stimuli.title: The Ditch That Built a Nation
stimuli.text:
In the early 1800s, moving goods across New York State was slow and costly. Wagons bumped over muddy roads, and shipping a ton of flour from Buffalo to New York City could take weeks. Governor DeWitt Clinton believed the answer was a canal: a waterway dug by hand that would link Lake Erie to the Hudson River.

Many people laughed at the idea. Newspapers called it "Clinton's Ditch." The canal would have to stretch about 363 miles, from Buffalo to Albany, and climb over hills using a series of locks, gated chambers that raise and lower boats. No one in the young country had attempted anything so large.

Work began in 1817. Crews of laborers, many of them recent immigrants, cleared forests and dug through rock with shovels, picks and blasting powder. When the Erie Canal opened in 1825, the doubters fell silent. Boats pulled by mules along a towpath could now carry goods across the state in a fraction of the time, and shipping costs dropped sharply.

The canal changed the map of the nation. Towns such as Rochester and Syracuse grew quickly along its banks, and New York City became the busiest port in the country. Farmers in the Midwest could now send their crops east, and settlers could travel west more easily. The "ditch" that people had mocked had become one of the most important routes in America.

stimuli.title: The Last Rehearsal
stimuli.text:
Priya stood in the wings, gripping the edge of the curtain so hard her knuckles turned pale. Out on the stage, the rest of the cast was running through the final scene for the last time before opening night. In ten minutes it would be her turn to walk out alone and sing.

"You've practiced this a hundred times," Mr. Alvarez whispered beside her. "Your voice knows the way even if your knees don't."

Priya tried to smile. Her mouth felt full of sand. She thought of the empty auditorium, its rows of red seats like rows of waiting faces, and her stomach did a slow flip.

Then the music started. For a heartbeat she could not move. But the first notes were the same notes she had hummed while washing dishes, while walking the dog, while lying awake at night, and her feet carried her forward before her worries could catch up. By the second verse, the seats were only seats again.

stimuli.title: Dancing Directions
stimuli.text:
A honeybee that finds a good patch of flowers faces a problem: how can she tell the other bees in her hive where to go? Bees cannot draw maps or speak, yet a returning forager can send her sisters to flowers more than a mile away. She does it by dancing.

Inside the dark hive, the forager walks in a straight line across the honeycomb while shaking her body from side to side. Then she circles back and repeats the move again and again. Scientists call this the waggle dance. The angle of the straight run tells the other bees which direction to fly, measured from the position of the sun. The length of the waggle tells them how far to go: the longer she waggles, the more distant the flowers.

The Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch spent years watching bees at glass-walled hives before he decoded the dance. Many scientists at first doubted that an insect could share such exact information. Von Frisch's careful experiments, in which he moved feeding dishes farther and farther away, convinced them. In 1973 he shared the Nobel Prize for his work.

Today, researchers still study the waggle dance. By filming dances and translating them, they can learn where bees in a city or on a farm are finding food, which helps people plant the flowers bees need most.

stimuli.title: Reading with Fingertips
stimuli.text:
Louis Braille was three years old when an accident in his father's leather workshop injured one of his eyes. An infection spread, and by age five he was completely blind. In France in the early 1800s, few blind children received any schooling, but Louis was bright and determined. At ten, he won a place at a school for blind students in Paris.

The school owned a few books printed with large raised letters. Reading them was painfully slow, because fingers cannot easily tell one curving letter from another. The books were also huge and heavy, and students could not write in that system at all.

Then a visitor brought news of "night writing," a code of raised dots that an army captain, Charles Barbier, had invented so soldiers could pass messages in the dark. Louis saw its promise at once, but Barbier's code used up to twelve dots for a single sound, too many for a fingertip to feel at one touch. Working on his own, the teenager simplified it. By the time he was fifteen, Louis had created a system in which each letter is made from a cell of just six dots, arranged in two columns of three.

Braille's code spread slowly at first; some teachers even banned it. But blind readers loved it, and long after his death it became the standard around the world. Today the same six-dot cell is used for many languages, for music and even for mathematics.

stimuli.title: Grandfather's Watch
stimuli.text:
The watch had not ticked in thirty years. It lay in a velvet box in the top drawer of my grandfather's desk, its glass cloudy, its hands frozen at twenty past four.

"Why don't you get it fixed?" I asked him once.

He turned the watch over in his rough palm as if it weighed a great deal more than it did. "It stopped the afternoon your grandmother and I opened the bakery," he said. "We were too busy to wind it that day, and the next, and the next. By the time we remembered, we had a business, a mortgage and a baby on the way." He laughed softly. "I suppose I like it the way it is. It reminds me of the day everything started."

He closed the lid, and I understood that some broken things are not waiting to be repaired.

stimuli.title: A Sea Where You Cannot Sink
stimuli.text:
Visitors to the Dead Sea, which lies between Israel and Jordan, like to take a strange photograph: a person lying back in the water, reading a newspaper, floating without any effort. The trick works because the Dead Sea is one of the saltiest bodies of water on Earth, almost ten times saltier than the ocean.

The reason lies in its location. The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest dry land on the planet, more than 1,300 feet below sea level. The Jordan River and smaller streams flow into it, but no river flows out. In the hot, dry climate, water leaves only by evaporating into the air. Each time water evaporates, the salt it carried stays behind, so over thousands of years the salt has built up.

All that salt makes the water much denser than fresh water, and a dense liquid pushes up harder on anything placed in it. That is why swimmers bob on the surface like corks. It is also why no fish live there. Only tiny bacteria and other microbes can survive.

Today the Dead Sea is shrinking. People take water from the Jordan River for farms and cities, so less reaches the sea, and its surface drops by about three feet a year. Scientists and the nearby countries are studying ways to slow the loss before more of this unusual sea disappears.

stimuli.title: First Snow
stimuli.text:
Mateo had lived his whole life in a town where winter meant a light jacket and the occasional cold drizzle. So when his family moved north in December, he spent the first week glaring at the gray sky as if it owed him something.

On Saturday he woke to a silence so complete that he thought his ears had stopped working. The street outside his window had vanished under a thick white blanket. Every car was a soft lump, every fence post wore a tall white hat.

He was outside before his mother could finish saying "boots." The snow squeaked under his sneakers and soaked his socks in seconds, but he did not care. He scooped up a handful and watched it sparkle, then melt into cold water in his palm. Down the street, a girl his age was rolling an enormous snowball. She looked up and waved. Mateo waved back, and for the first time since the move, the new town did not feel quite so far from home.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Oak, maple and birch are all trees. A tulip is a flower.

questions.stem: Which word means the same as **reluctant**?
questions.explanation: Someone reluctant does not want to do something, so they are unwilling. Unaware means not knowing, which is a different idea.

questions.stem: Maria is taller than Jon. Jon is taller than Lee. Maria is taller than Lee. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: Maria is taller than Jon, and Jon is taller than Lee, so Maria must also be taller than Lee.

questions.stem: Which word means the opposite of **generous**?
questions.explanation: A generous person gives freely; a stingy person hates to give anything away. Wealthy describes how much someone has, not how they share it.

questions.stem: **Pilot** is to **airplane** as **captain** is to:
questions.explanation: A pilot is in charge of flying an airplane, and a captain is in charge of a ship. The crew works for the captain; it is not what the captain commands in the same way.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: A violin, a cello and a harp are all played by moving strings. A flute is a wind instrument.

questions.stem: **Abundant** most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Abundant means there is a great deal of something, or plenty. Scarce is the opposite: there is very little.

questions.stem: All the books on the top shelf are mysteries. The red book is on the top shelf. The red book is a mystery. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: Every book on the top shelf is a mystery, and the red book is on that shelf, so it must be a mystery.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: A triangle, a square and a pentagon are all made of straight sides. A circle has no straight sides.

questions.stem: **Expand** is the opposite of:
questions.explanation: To expand is to grow larger, so the opposite is to shrink. Stretch is close to expand in meaning, not opposite.

questions.stem: **Thermometer** is to **temperature** as **scale** is to:
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature, and a scale measures weight. Height is measured with a ruler or tape measure.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Whisper, murmur and mumble are all ways of speaking quietly. To shout is to speak loudly.

questions.stem: Which word means the same as **candid**?
questions.explanation: A candid answer is open and honest, which is what frank means. It has nothing to do with candy or sweetness.

questions.stem: Sam runs faster than Ava. Kim runs faster than Ava. Sam runs faster than Kim. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: Both Sam and Kim are faster than Ava, but nothing compares Sam with Kim. Either one could be faster, so the statement is uncertain.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Ancient, antique and aged all describe something old. Modern describes something new.

questions.stem: Which word means the opposite of **conceal**?
questions.explanation: To conceal is to hide, so the opposite is to reveal, or show. Disguise is another way of hiding, so it is a near synonym.

questions.stem: **Drought** is to **water** as **famine** is to:
questions.explanation: A drought is a serious lack of water, and a famine is a serious lack of food. Hunger is what a famine causes, not what is missing.

questions.stem: **Meticulous** most nearly means:
questions.explanation: A meticulous worker pays close attention to every detail, so meticulous means very careful. Hurried work is the opposite of meticulous work.

questions.stem: A pen costs more than a pencil. A pencil costs more than an eraser. An eraser costs more than a pen. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: The pen costs more than the pencil, which costs more than the eraser, so the pen costs more than the eraser. The third statement says the reverse, so it is false.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Furious, irate and enraged all mean very angry. Content means calm and satisfied.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 3, 7, 11, 15, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is 4 more than the one before it: 15 + 4 = 19.

questions.stem: What number is 5 more than 3/4 of 20?
questions.explanation: 3/4 of 20 is 15, and 15 + 5 = 20. Stopping at 15 leaves out the 5.

questions.stem: A square has sides 5 cm long. Compare (I) its perimeter in centimeters, (II) its area in square centimeters and (III) the length of one side in centimeters. Which is true?
questions.explanation: The perimeter is 4 × 5 = 20, the area is 5 × 5 = 25 and a side is 5. So II (25) > I (20) > III (5).

questions.stem: Compare (I) 0.5, (II) 1/2 and (III) 50%. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 0.5, 1/2 and 50% are three ways of writing the same amount, one half.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 2, 6, 18, 54, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is 3 times the one before it: 54 × 3 = 162. Adding the last gap of 36 again would give 90 instead.

questions.stem: What is 1/3 of the sum of 17 and 19?
questions.explanation: The sum is 17 + 19 = 36, and 1/3 of 36 is 12. Half of 36 would be 18.

questions.stem: Rectangle ABCD is 8 inches long (AB) and 6 inches wide (BC), and AC is a diagonal. Which is true?
questions.explanation: The diagonal makes a right triangle with sides 6 and 8, so AC = 10. AB + BC = 14 and AB = 8, so 14 > 10 > 8. Going around two sides is always longer than cutting across.

questions.stem: Compare (I) 3², (II) 2³ and (III) 4 + 4. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 3² = 3 × 3 = 9, 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 and 4 + 4 = 8. So I is greatest and II equals III.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 50, 46, 43, 41, ...?
questions.explanation: The amount subtracted goes down by one each time: minus 4, minus 3, minus 2, then minus 1. So 41 - 1 = 40.

questions.stem: What number divided by 4 is equal to 9 less than 20?
questions.explanation: 9 less than 20 is 11. The number divided by 4 gives 11, so the number is 11 × 4 = 44.

questions.stem: A circle has a radius of 3 units. Compare (I) its diameter, (II) its radius and (III) its circumference, using 3.14 for pi. Which is true?
questions.explanation: The diameter is 2 × 3 = 6 and the circumference is 3.14 × 6, about 18.8. So III (18.8) > I (6) > II (3).

questions.stem: Compare (I) 20% of 60, (II) 1/3 of 36 and (III) 0.4 × 25. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 20% of 60 is 12, 1/3 of 36 is 12 and 0.4 × 25 is 10. So I and II are equal and greater than III.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...?
questions.explanation: These are the square numbers 1 × 1, 2 × 2, 3 × 3, 4 × 4 and 5 × 5. The next is 6 × 6 = 36. The gaps (3, 5, 7, 9) also grow by 2, giving 25 + 11 = 36.

questions.stem: What number is 40% of the product of 5 and 6?
questions.explanation: The product of 5 and 6 is 30, and 40% of 30 is 0.4 × 30 = 12. Half of 30 would be 15.

questions.stem: In triangle PQR, angle P is 90° and angle Q is 35°. Which is true?
options: Angle Q is greater than angle R
Angle R is equal to angle Q
Angle R is greater than angle P
Angle R is greater than angle Q
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°, so angle R = 180 - 90 - 35 = 55°. That is more than 35° but less than 90°.

questions.stem: Compare (I) 15 - (-3), (II) -15 + 3 and (III) the absolute value of -15. Which is true?
questions.explanation: Subtracting -3 is adding 3, so I is 18. II is -12, and the absolute value of -15 is 15. So 18 > 15 > -12.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 5, 10, 8, 16, 14, ...?
questions.explanation: The pattern is multiply by 2, then subtract 2: 5, 10, 8, 16, 14, and then 14 × 2 = 28. Subtracting 2 again would give 12, but that step comes after the doubling.

questions.stem: What number subtracted from 50 leaves 3 more than the product of 4 and 7?
questions.explanation: The product of 4 and 7 is 28, and 3 more is 31. The number taken from 50 must leave 31, so it is 50 - 31 = 19.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __brief__ meeting"?
questions.explanation: A brief meeting does not last long, so brief means short.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "__gather__ the papers"?
questions.explanation: To gather papers is to collect them into one place. Divide means the opposite.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the main idea of the passage?
options: A mocked project became a vital route
Mules once pulled boats across New York
New York was hard to cross on foot
questions.explanation: The passage follows the canal from a project people laughed at to one of the most important routes in America. The mules are only one detail.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what is a lock?
options: A dam that blocks a river
A gate that charged a toll
questions.explanation: The second paragraph defines locks as gated chambers that raise and lower boats. The path for the mules is the towpath.

questions.stem: Why did newspapers most likely call the project "Clinton's Ditch"?
options: To make fun of the plan
To name the town it started in
questions.explanation: The passage says many people laughed at the idea, and later that the doubters fell silent. Calling a huge canal a ditch was a way of mocking it.

questions.stem: In the third paragraph, the phrase "in a fraction of the time" means:
questions.explanation: A fraction is a small part, so a trip that takes a fraction of the time is much quicker. The paragraph adds that shipping costs dropped too.

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, which was a result of the canal?
options: Buffalo replaced Albany as the capital
Wagon roads across New York improved
Midwest farmers could ship crops east
Ships could sail from the ocean to Ohio
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says farmers in the Midwest could now send their crops east. The passage never mentions better roads or a new capital.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __lenient__ teacher"?
questions.explanation: A lenient teacher is not strict and lets small mistakes go, so lenient means forgiving. Demanding is the opposite.

questions.stem: How does Priya feel at the start of the passage?
questions.explanation: She grips the curtain until her knuckles turn pale and her stomach flips. These details show nerves, not anger or boredom.

questions.stem: What does Mr. Alvarez mean when he says, "Your voice knows the way even if your knees don't"?
options: She should sit down before singing
Her singing still needs more work
Her practice will see her through
She will forget the words tonight
questions.explanation: He reminds her she has practiced a hundred times, so her singing will come even though she feels shaky. Her knees stand for her nerves.

questions.stem: The last sentence, "the seats were only seats again," shows that Priya:
questions.explanation: Earlier the seats looked like waiting faces because she was scared. Once she is singing, they are just seats, so her fear is gone.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __imitate__ a bird call"?
questions.explanation: To imitate a sound is to copy it. You can record a bird call without imitating it.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __hazardous__ trail"?
questions.explanation: A hazard is a danger, so a hazardous trail is a dangerous one. A winding trail may or may not be dangerous.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How bees share where food is
Why bees need flowers to survive
How a hive stays dark inside
questions.explanation: The passage explains the waggle dance, the way a forager tells other bees where to find flowers, and how it was discovered.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what does the length of the waggle tell the other bees?
options: Which way to fly from the sun
How many flowers are in bloom
How far away the flowers are
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says the longer the waggle, the more distant the flowers. The direction comes from the angle of the run, not its length.

questions.stem: Why does the author describe von Frisch moving feeding dishes farther away?
options: To show how bees find new hives
To show how he proved his idea
To explain why bees fly at night
To describe how bees make honey
questions.explanation: The paragraph says many scientists doubted him until his careful experiments with the dishes convinced them. The detail shows how he proved what the dance means.

questions.stem: Which statement would the author most likely agree with?
options: Bee research can help real gardens
Bees only dance on sunny days
Von Frisch's ideas are now doubted
Bees learn the dance from people
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says decoding dances helps people plant the flowers bees need most. It says scientists were convinced, not that they doubt him today.

questions.stem: In the third paragraph, the word "decoded" means:
questions.explanation: To decode is to figure out what a code or signal means. Von Frisch worked out what each part of the dance tells the bees.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "an __obstinate__ mule"?
questions.explanation: An obstinate mule refuses to do what it is told, so obstinate means stubborn. Obedient means the opposite.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __alleviate__ the pain"?
questions.explanation: To alleviate pain is to make it less severe, or ease it. To cause pain is the opposite.

questions.stem: What is 3/4 + 5/6?
questions.explanation: Use twelfths: 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12, so the sum is 19/12 = 1 7/12. Adding tops and bottoms to get 8/10 does not work.

questions.stem: What is the area of a triangle with a base of 12 cm and a height of 7 cm?
questions.explanation: Area = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 12 × 7 = 42. Forgetting the 1/2 gives 84.

questions.stem: What is 0.6 × 0.4?
questions.explanation: 6 × 4 = 24, and the two factors have two decimal places in all, so the product is 0.24.

questions.stem: If 3x + 7 = 25, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides to get 3x = 18, then divide by 3: x = 6. Stopping at 18 forgets to divide.

questions.stem: What is the mean of 6, 15, 9, 20 and 10?
questions.explanation: The sum is 6 + 15 + 9 + 20 + 10 = 60, and 60 ÷ 5 = 12. 10 is the median, the middle number in order.

questions.stem: What is the greatest common factor of 36 and 60?
questions.explanation: 36 = 12 × 3 and 60 = 12 × 5, and 3 and 5 share no factor, so 12 is the greatest common factor. 180 is their least common multiple.

questions.stem: How many inches are in 2 1/2 yards?
questions.explanation: One yard is 36 inches, so 2 1/2 yards is 2.5 × 36 = 90 inches. 30 inches is 2 1/2 feet.

questions.stem: A jacket that costs \$80 is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: 25% of \$80 is \$20, so the sale price is \$80 - \$20 = \$60. \$20 is the discount, not the price.

questions.stem: Two angles of a triangle measure 48° and 67°. What is the measure of the third angle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add to 180°: 180 - 48 - 67 = 65. 115° is the sum of the two given angles.

questions.stem: What is 4.07 × 10³?
questions.explanation: Multiplying by 10³, or 1,000, moves the decimal point three places to the right: 4.07 becomes 4,070.

questions.stem: What is the value of 2a² - b when a = 3 and b = 4?
questions.explanation: Square first: a² = 9, so 2a² = 18, and 18 - 4 = 14. Doubling before squaring gives (2 × 3)² - 4 = 32.

questions.stem: A bag holds 4 red, 5 blue and 3 green marbles. One marble is drawn without looking. What is the probability that it is blue?
questions.explanation: There are 4 + 5 + 3 = 12 marbles and 5 of them are blue, so the probability is 5/12. 5/7 compares blue with the other marbles instead of with all of them.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for every 2 cups of sugar. How many cups of flour are needed with 8 cups of sugar?
questions.explanation: 8 cups of sugar is 4 times the 2 cups in the recipe, so use 4 × 3 = 12 cups of flour. Adding 3 to 8 to get 11 treats the ratio as a difference.

questions.stem: Using 22/7 for pi, what is the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 14 inches?
questions.explanation: Circumference = pi × diameter = 22/7 × 14 = 44 inches. 154 is the area of that circle in square inches.
Multiply first: 3 × (-2) = -6. Then -8 + (-6) = -14. Adding first gives (-5) × (-2) = 10, which breaks the order of operations.

questions.stem: What is the square root of 81 plus 2³?
questions.explanation: The square root of 81 is 9, and 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, so the total is 17. Reading 2³ as 2 × 3 gives 15.

questions.stem: A movie starts at 7:45 p.m. and lasts 1 hour 50 minutes. At what time does it end?
questions.explanation: One hour after 7:45 is 8:45, and 50 more minutes is 9:35. Forgetting to carry the extra hour past 60 minutes gives 8:35.

questions.stem: Which inequality says that a number n is at least 12?
questions.explanation: At least 12 means 12 or more, so n can equal 12: n ≥ 12. The symbol > would leave out 12 itself.

questions.stem: Five test scores are 78, 85, 92, 85 and 70. What is their range?
questions.explanation: The range is the highest score minus the lowest: 92 - 70 = 22. 82 is the mean and 85 is the median and mode.

questions.stem: What is the least common multiple of 8 and 12?
questions.explanation: The multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36 and so on, and 24 is the first one 8 divides evenly. 4 is the greatest common factor, and 96 is simply 8 × 12.

questions.stem: A box is 5 ft long, 3 ft wide and 4 ft high. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume = length × width × height = 5 × 3 × 4 = 60 cubic feet. 94 is the box's surface area in square feet.

questions.stem: What is 2/3 ÷ 4/9?
questions.explanation: Multiply by the reciprocal: 2/3 × 9/4 = 18/12 = 3/2 = 1 1/2. Multiplying straight across gives 8/27.

questions.stem: Ramon studied for weeks; ___, he passed the test easily. Which word or words best join the ideas?
questions.explanation: Passing easily is the result of studying for weeks, so as a result shows the link. However would signal a contrast.

questions.stem: Yesterday the team ___ for two hours. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: Yesterday points to a finished action in the past, so the simple past practiced fits.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: After the game, we went out for pizza.
After the game we went, out for pizza.
After, the game we went out for pizza.
After the game we went out, for pizza.
questions.explanation: A comma follows an introductory phrase such as After the game. The other commas break up words that belong together.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Receive follows the rule i before e except after c: the c is followed by ei.

questions.passage: (1) Sea otters live along the coast of the northern Pacific Ocean. (2) They use rocks as tools to crack open clams and other shellfish. (3) Many people enjoy visiting the beach in summer. (4) Otters often float on their backs while they eat.
questions.stem: Which sentence does not belong in this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The paragraph is about sea otters. Sentence 3 is about people at the beach, so it does not belong.

questions.stem: Of the three paintings, this one is the ___. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: Comparing three or more things takes the superlative, and a long adjective uses most: most colorful. More colorful compares only two.

questions.stem: Which sentence expresses the idea most clearly?
options: Tired from the hike, the stream was where we rested.
We rested, tired, by the stream, from the hike.
Tired from the hike, we rested by the stream.
By the stream tired from the hike rested we.
questions.explanation: Tired from the hike describes the people, so we must come right after it. Putting the stream there makes it sound as if the stream was tired.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
options: We visited uncle Ray in Denver last July.
We visited Uncle Ray in denver last July.
We visited Uncle Ray in Denver last July.
We visited Uncle Ray in Denver last july.
questions.explanation: Uncle is capitalized when it is used as part of a name, and the names of cities and months are always capitalized.

questions.stem: The new bike rides ___ over rough trails. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: The word tells how the bike rides, so it must be the adverb smoothly. Smooth is an adjective that describes a noun.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Necessary has one c and two s's. A memory trick: one collar and two sleeves.

questions.passage: ___ Aluminum cans can be melted down and made into new cans. Old newspapers can be turned into fresh paper, which saves trees. Plastic bottles can even become fleece jackets.
questions.stem: Which sentence would be the best topic sentence for this paragraph?
options: Aluminum is a very light metal to use.
Fleece jackets keep people warm in winter.
Trees grow slowly in cold places.
Recycling turns old things into new ones.
questions.explanation: Every detail shows something old being made into something new, so a sentence about recycling covers them all. The other sentences each fit only one detail, or none.

questions.stem: Neither of the boys ___ his science project yet. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: Neither means not one of the two, so it is singular and takes has. The phrase of the boys does not change the subject.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The two girl's bikes were locked outside.
The two girls' bikes were locked outside.
The two girls bike's were locked outside.
The two girls's bikes were locked outside.
questions.explanation: To show that more than one girl owns something, add only an apostrophe after the s: girls'. Girl's would mean just one girl.

questions.passage: The museum opens at nine. It closes at five.
questions.stem: Which sentence best combines these two sentences?
options: The museum opens at nine, it closes at five.
The museum, it opens at nine and at five closes.
The museum opens at nine and closes at five.
Opening at nine, five is when the museum closes.
questions.explanation: Joining the two verbs with and makes one smooth sentence. Joining two sentences with only a comma is a comma splice.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: The coach gave Jamal and I new jerseys.
The coach gave Jamal and myself new jerseys.
The coach gave Jamal and me new jerseys.
The coach gave him and I new jerseys.
questions.explanation: After a verb such as gave, use me. Try it alone: the coach gave me new jerseys, not gave I. Myself is used only when the subject did the action.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written most clearly, with no extra words?
options: We returned back home at noon.
We returned home at 12 noon midday.
At noon we returned, at noon, home.
questions.explanation: Returned already means came back, so back is not needed, and noon already means 12 midday. Saying a thing twice adds nothing.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Embarrass has a double r and a double s, and it begins with em.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: Bring three things; a pencil, an eraser, and a ruler.
Bring: three things a pencil, an eraser, and a ruler.
Bring three things, a pencil: an eraser, and a ruler.
Bring three things: a pencil, an eraser, and a ruler.
questions.explanation: A colon can introduce a list after a complete thought such as Bring three things. A semicolon joins two complete sentences, not a sentence and a list.

questions.stem: Our cat likes to ___ in the sunny window. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: Lie means to rest, and it takes no object. Lay means to put something down, so it needs an object: lay the book on the table.

questions.stem: The trail was steep and rocky; ___, the view from the top made the climb worthwhile. Which word or words best join the ideas?
questions.explanation: The second idea goes against what you might expect from a hard trail, so it needs a contrast word such as nevertheless. Therefore would mean the view was caused by the rocks.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus and Mars are planets that orbit the sun. The Moon orbits Earth.

questions.stem: Which word means the same as **vacant**?
questions.explanation: A vacant seat or house has no one in it, so it is empty. A quiet house may still have people inside.

questions.stem: No reptiles have feathers. A gecko is a reptile. A gecko has feathers. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: If no reptile has feathers and a gecko is a reptile, then a gecko cannot have feathers. The third statement is false.

questions.stem: Which word means the opposite of **ancient**?
questions.explanation: Ancient means very old, from long ago, so the opposite is modern. A ruin may be ancient, but ruined is not an opposite.

questions.stem: **Petal** is to **flower** as **page** is to:
questions.explanation: A petal is one part of a flower, and a page is one part of a book. A word is a part of a page, which reverses the relationship.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Sprint, dash and race all mean to move very fast. To stroll is to walk slowly.

questions.stem: **Hostile** most nearly means:
questions.explanation: A hostile crowd or reply is unfriendly, even angry. Unfamiliar means not known, which is a different idea.

questions.stem: The library opens before the bank. The bakery opens after the bank. The bakery opens before the library. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: The order is library, then bank, then bakery. The bakery opens after the library, so the third statement is false.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Brave, bold and fearless all describe someone without fear. Timid describes someone easily frightened.

questions.stem: **Timid** is the opposite of:
questions.explanation: A timid person is easily frightened; a bold person is daring. Shy means nearly the same as timid.

questions.stem: **Hive** is to **bee** as **nest** is to:
questions.explanation: A bee lives in a hive, and a bird lives in a nest. An egg is kept in a nest, but it is not the animal that builds and lives in it.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Copper, aluminum and silver are all metals. Granite is a kind of rock.

questions.stem: Which word means the same as **diligent**?
questions.explanation: A diligent student keeps working steadily and carefully, so diligent means hardworking. Quick-witted describes how fast someone thinks, not how hard they work.

questions.stem: Ella lives east of Ray. Ray lives east of Tom. Tom lives west of Ella. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: From west to east the order is Tom, Ray, Ella. Tom is west of Ella, so the third statement is true.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: A centimeter, a kilometer and a millimeter all measure length. A kilogram measures mass.

questions.stem: Which word means the opposite of **scarce**?
questions.explanation: Scarce means there is very little of something, so the opposite is plentiful. Rare means nearly the same as scarce.

questions.stem: **Cautious** is to **reckless** as **humble** is to:
questions.explanation: Cautious and reckless are opposites, so the answer must be the opposite of humble, which is arrogant. Modest means nearly the same as humble.

questions.stem: **Ambiguous** most nearly means:
questions.explanation: An ambiguous sentence can be read more than one way, so its meaning is unclear. An ambiguous statement is not necessarily untrue.

questions.stem: Some students in the band play drums. Owen is in the band. Owen plays drums. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: Only some band members play drums, so knowing Owen is in the band does not tell us whether he is one of them. The statement is uncertain.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Frugal, thrifty and economical all describe careful spending. Lavish describes spending freely and generously.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 64, 32, 16, 8, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is half of the one before it: 8 ÷ 2 = 4.

questions.stem: What number is 8 less than 2/5 of 45?
A cube has edges 2 cm long. Compare (I) the number of its faces, (II) its volume in cubic centimeters and (III) the number of its edges. Which is true?
questions.explanation: A cube has 6 faces and 12 edges, and its volume is 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. So III (12) > II (8) > I (6).

questions.stem: Compare (I) 7 × 8, (II) 6 × 9 and (III) 4 × 14. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 7 × 8 = 56, 6 × 9 = 54 and 4 × 14 = 56. So I and III are equal and greater than II.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 7, 12, 17, 22, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is 5 more than the one before it: 22 + 5 = 27.

questions.stem: What number is twice the difference between 30 and 17?
questions.explanation: The difference between 30 and 17 is 13, and twice 13 is 26. Twice the sum would be 94.

questions.stem: Two straight lines cross. One of the four angles they make is 70°. Angle X is directly across from that angle, and angle Y is right next to it. Which is true?
options: Angle Y is greater than angle X
Angle X is greater than angle Y
Angle X is equal to angle Y
Angles X and Y add up to 90°
questions.explanation: Vertical angles are equal, so X = 70°. Angles side by side on a straight line add to 180°, so Y = 110°. Y is greater, and X + Y = 180°, not 90°.

questions.stem: Compare (I) 1/4 + 1/4, (II) 1/4 × 4 and (III) 1/4 ÷ 1/2. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2, 1/4 × 4 = 1 and 1/4 ÷ 1/2 = 1/4 × 2 = 1/2. So II is greatest and I equals III.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21. Doubling 13 to get 26 does not fit the earlier terms.

questions.stem: What number multiplied by 6 is 12 more than 30?
questions.explanation: 12 more than 30 is 42, and 42 ÷ 6 = 7. Using 12 less than 30 would give 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

questions.stem: A triangle has a base of 10 and a height of 6. A rectangle has a base of 5 and a height of 6. Which is true?
options: The triangle has half the area
questions.explanation: The triangle's area is 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 and the rectangle's is 5 × 6 = 30. Half the base of the triangle makes up for the 1/2 in its formula.

questions.stem: Compare (I) 0.3, (II) 0.03 × 10 and (III) 3/8. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 0.03 × 10 = 0.3, so I equals II. 3/8 = 0.375, which is greater than 0.3.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 81, 27, 9, 3, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is the one before it divided by 3: 3 ÷ 3 = 1. One third would be the term after that.

questions.stem: What is 25% of the product of 8 and 9?
questions.explanation: The product is 8 × 9 = 72, and 25% is one fourth: 72 ÷ 4 = 18. Half of 72 is 36.

questions.stem: Rectangle A is 9 m long and 4 m wide. Square B has sides 6 m long. Which is true?
options: Same area; B has the longer perimeter
A has more area; same perimeter
B has more area; same perimeter
Same area; A has the longer perimeter
questions.explanation: Both areas are 36 square meters (9 × 4 and 6 × 6). The perimeters are 2 × (9 + 4) = 26 m for A and 4 × 6 = 24 m for B.

questions.stem: Compare (I) 2⁵, (II) 5² and (III) 3³. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 2⁵ = 32, 5² = 25 and 3³ = 27. So 32 > 27 > 25. Mixing up the base and the exponent is the usual mistake.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 4, 7, 13, 25, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is double the one before it, minus 1: 4 × 2 - 1 = 7, 7 × 2 - 1 = 13, 13 × 2 - 1 = 25, so 25 × 2 - 1 = 49. Forgetting to subtract 1 gives 50.

questions.stem: If 7 is added to a number and the result is tripled, the answer is 45. What is the number?
questions.explanation: Work backward: 45 ÷ 3 = 15, then 15 - 7 = 8. Check: (8 + 7) × 3 = 45.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __damp__ towel"?
questions.explanation: A damp towel is slightly wet, or moist.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __halt__ the game"?
questions.explanation: To halt something is to stop it. Start means the opposite.

questions.stem: What happened right after Louis heard about "night writing"?
options: He made a simpler dot code
He was injured in the workshop
He won a place at the school
questions.explanation: After learning of Barbier's code, Louis saw its promise and simplified it into his six-dot cell. The injury and the school came earlier.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what was wrong with Barbier's code for reading?
options: It was printed in huge books
It could not be written at all
Too many dots for one sound
questions.explanation: The passage says the code used up to twelve dots for one sound, too many to feel at one touch. The huge books were the raised-letter books.

questions.stem: Why was reading the school's raised-letter books so slow?
options: The students were not allowed to
The books were written in code
The letters were too small to see
questions.explanation: The second paragraph says fingers cannot easily tell one curving letter from another. The students read by touch, not by sight.

questions.stem: The detail that some teachers banned Braille's code suggests that:
options: his code was hard for students
the code worked only in French
questions.explanation: Teachers banned it even though blind readers loved it, which shows the new system was not welcomed at first. The passage says readers loved it, so they did not dislike it.

questions.stem: Which title would also fit this passage?
options: Life in an Army Camp at Night
How Books Were Printed in Old Paris
A Teen Changes How the Blind Read
questions.explanation: The passage tells how Louis, as a teenager, created the code blind readers still use. The workshop and the army are only details.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __fragrant__ garden"?
questions.explanation: Fragrant describes a pleasant smell, so a fragrant garden is sweet-smelling. Bright colors are seen, not smelled.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why did the watch first stop?
options: It fell on the bakery floor
A child dropped it in the desk
Its glass cracked in the drawer
No one wound it on a busy day
questions.explanation: Grandfather says they were too busy opening the bakery to wind it, that day and the days after. Nothing in the passage says it was dropped.

questions.stem: Why does the grandfather keep the watch unrepaired?
options: It would cost too much to fix
He has forgotten how to wind it
It recalls the day it all began
He plans to sell it to a collector
questions.explanation: He says he likes it that way because it reminds him of the day everything started. He never mentions money or selling it.

questions.stem: Which sentence best states the theme of the passage?
options: An object can hold precious memories
Old things should always be repaired
Running a business takes hard work
Watches were better in the past
questions.explanation: The narrator learns that some broken things are not waiting to be repaired because they hold memories. Hard work is part of the story but not its lesson.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __postpone__ the trip"?
questions.explanation: To postpone a trip is to put it off until later, or delay it. A canceled trip does not happen at all.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __vivid__ dream"?
questions.explanation: A vivid dream is bright and clear, as if it were real. A vivid dream can be pleasant, so it is not necessarily scary.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to swim safely in the sea
Why the Dead Sea is so salty
Which fish live in salt water
questions.explanation: Most of the passage explains how salt builds up in the Dead Sea and what that salt does. The other choices are not discussed or are only details.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why has salt built up in the Dead Sea?
options: Salt is mined along its shore
questions.explanation: No river flows out, so water leaves only by evaporating, and each time the salt stays behind. No ocean water flows in.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what lives in the Dead Sea?
questions.explanation: The third paragraph says no fish live there and only tiny bacteria and other microbes can survive. Saying nothing lives there goes too far.

questions.stem: In the third paragraph, the word "denser" means:
questions.explanation: A denser liquid packs more matter into the same space, so a cup of it is heavier. That is why it pushes swimmers up so strongly.

questions.stem: Based on the last paragraph, which would most likely help the Dead Sea?
options: Adding more salt to its water
Digging a river to drain it
questions.explanation: The sea is shrinking because people take water from the Jordan River before it arrives. Letting more of that water reach the sea would slow the loss.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __novice__ skier"?
questions.explanation: A novice is someone new to an activity, so a novice skier is a beginner. A champion is the opposite.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __meager__ meal"?
questions.explanation: A meager meal is too small or barely enough. It says nothing about taste or cost.

questions.stem: What is 6.4827 rounded to the nearest hundredth?
questions.explanation: The hundredths digit is 8, and the next digit, 2, is less than 5, so it stays 6.48. 6.483 is rounded to the nearest thousandth.

questions.stem: Using 3.14 for pi, what is the area of a circle with a radius of 5 m?
questions.explanation: Area = pi × radius² = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5. 31.4 is the circumference in meters.

questions.stem: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 29 has no factors except 1 and itself. 21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3 × 9 and 33 = 3 × 11.

questions.stem: Which expression is equal to 4x + 3y - x + 2y?
questions.explanation: Combine the x terms (4x - x = 3x) and the y terms (3y + 2y = 5y) to get 3x + 5y.

questions.stem: What is the median of 3, 8, 11, 4, 7 and 15?
questions.explanation: In order the numbers are 3, 4, 7, 8, 11, 15. With six numbers, the median is halfway between the middle two: (7 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.5. 8 is the mean.

questions.stem: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. At the same speed, how far will it travel in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: The car goes 150 ÷ 3 = 50 miles each hour, so in 5 hours it goes 5 × 50 = 250 miles.

questions.stem: How many milliliters are in 3.2 liters?
questions.explanation: One liter is 1,000 milliliters, so 3.2 liters is 3,200 milliliters.

questions.stem: What is 15% of 240?
A right triangle has legs 9 units and 12 units long. How long is its hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, and the square root of 225 is 15. Adding the legs gives 21, which is too long.

questions.stem: What is the value of 3⁴?
questions.explanation: 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. Multiplying 3 × 4 gives 12, which is not the same thing.

questions.stem: If 5(n - 2) = 35, what is the value of n?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 5 to get n - 2 = 7, so n = 9. Stopping at 7 forgets to add the 2 back.

questions.stem: A fair coin is flipped twice. What is the probability of getting heads both times?
questions.explanation: Each flip has a 1/2 chance of heads, so two heads in a row is 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. The four equally likely results are HH, HT, TH and TT.
Change to improper fractions: 5/2 × 4/3 = 20/6 = 3 1/3. Multiplying only the whole numbers and the fractions separately gives 2 1/6.

questions.stem: The perimeter of a square is 36 inches. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 inches, so the area is 9 × 9 = 81 square inches. 9 is only the side length.

questions.stem: What is 7.2 ÷ 0.08?
questions.explanation: Move both decimal points two places: 720 ÷ 8 = 90.
(-6) × (-4) = 24, and 24 ÷ (-3) = -8. An odd number of negative signs makes the answer negative.

questions.stem: How many 1-pint jars can be filled from 3 gallons of lemonade?
questions.explanation: A gallon is 4 quarts and a quart is 2 pints, so a gallon is 8 pints. 3 gallons is 3 × 8 = 24 pints. 12 is the number of quarts.

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line through the points (1, 2) and (3, 8)?
questions.explanation: Slope = change in y ÷ change in x = (8 - 2) ÷ (3 - 1) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3. Dividing the other way gives 1/3.

questions.passage:
| Day | Items sold |
|---|---|
| Monday | 40 |
| Tuesday | 25 |
| Wednesday | 35 |
| Thursday | 50 |
questions.stem: A store's sales for four days are shown in the table. What percent of the four days' sales were on Thursday?
questions.explanation: The total is 40 + 25 + 35 + 50 = 150, and 50 out of 150 is 1/3, or 33 1/3%. 50% would compare Thursday with 100 items, not the total.

questions.stem: Sales tax is 6%. What is the total cost of a \$45 item, including tax?
What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: A hexagon's angles add to (6 - 2) × 180 = 720°, and 720 ÷ 6 = 120°. 108° is the angle of a regular pentagon.

questions.stem: The ratio of boys to girls in a club is 3 to 5. If the club has 40 members, how many are girls?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 3 + 5 = 8 parts, so each part is 40 ÷ 8 = 5 members. Girls are 5 parts: 5 × 5 = 25. Boys would be 15.

questions.stem: Most birds can fly. Penguins, ___, swim instead. Which word or words best join the ideas?
questions.explanation: Penguins are an exception to most birds, so the sentence needs a contrast word such as however.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: We don't have any milk left.
We don't have no milk left.
We doesn't have any milk left.
We don't have none milk left.
questions.explanation: Don't already makes the sentence negative, so use any, not no. We takes don't, not doesn't.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
options: Our class toured the Lincoln Memorial on Friday.
Our class toured the lincoln Memorial on Friday.
Our class toured the Lincoln memorial on Friday.
Our class toured the Lincoln Memorial on friday.
questions.explanation: Lincoln Memorial is the name of a particular place, so both words are capitalized, and so are the days of the week.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Separate has a in the middle: sep-a-rate. A memory trick: there is a rat in separate.

questions.passage: (1) Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the sky. (2) It heats the air around it so quickly that the air expands with a boom. (3) That boom is the thunder we hear. (4) My cousin is afraid of loud noises.
questions.stem: Which sentence does not belong in this paragraph?
questions.explanation: The paragraph explains what causes thunder. Sentence 4 is about a cousin, not about lightning or thunder.

questions.stem: The players packed ___ bags after practice. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: Their shows that the bags belong to the players. There names a place, and they're means they are.

questions.passage: Maya plays the trumpet. She plays it in the school band.
questions.stem: Which sentence best combines these two sentences?
options: Maya plays the trumpet, she plays in the band.
Maya plays the trumpet, and in the school band.
Playing the trumpet, the band has Maya in it.
Maya plays the trumpet in the school band.
questions.explanation: Adding in the school band to the first sentence says everything once. Joining two sentences with only a comma is a comma splice.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: In American English, the comma that ends a quotation goes inside the closing quotation mark, and the sentence still needs a period at the end.

questions.stem: The box of old letters ___ in the attic last spring. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: The subject is box, which is singular, so it takes was. The phrase of old letters does not change the subject.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Begin ends in one vowel and one consonant with the stress at the end, so the n is doubled before -ing: beginning.

questions.stem: Which sentence expresses the idea most clearly?
options: We saw a deer from the car with long antlers.
With long antlers, we saw a deer from the car.
From the car, we saw a deer with long antlers.
A deer from the car we saw with long antlers.
questions.explanation: With long antlers must sit next to deer. In the other sentences it seems to describe the car or the people.

questions.stem: Which of these is a complete sentence?
options: Barking at the mail carrier all day.
Because the dog barked at the carrier.
The dog that barked at the carrier.
The dog barked at the mail carrier.
questions.explanation: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb and expresses a full thought. The others are missing a main verb or begin with because and leave the thought unfinished.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: The bus was late so, we walked to school.
The bus, was late so we walked to school.
The bus was late, so, we walked to school.
The bus was late, so we walked to school.
questions.explanation: When so joins two complete sentences, the comma goes before so. No comma belongs between the subject and its verb.

questions.passage: Our school garden has changed lunchtime. Students grow tomatoes, beans and lettuce, and the cafeteria serves them in salads. Kids who once refused vegetables now ask for seconds of the food they planted themselves.
questions.stem: Which sentence would best conclude this paragraph?
options: Tomatoes need plenty of sun to ripen fully.
The garden made students eager to eat well.
Some students like to eat their lunch outside.
The cafeteria also sells milk and fruit juice.
questions.explanation: A concluding sentence sums up the main idea, which is that the garden changed how students eat. The others add new, smaller details.

questions.stem: To ___ should I give this note? Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: After a preposition such as to, use whom. Answer the question to check: give it to him, and him matches whom.

questions.stem: Which sentence best supports the idea that bicycles are good for busy cities?
options: Some bikes have a bell on the handlebars.
The first bicycles were built in the 1800s.
Bikes need far less road space than cars.
Many people like to ride bikes on weekends.
questions.explanation: A city with crowded roads benefits from vehicles that need less space. The other sentences are true of bikes but say nothing about cities.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Rhythm has no vowel other than the y: r-h-y-t-h-m.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: Its cold, so the dog stays in its bed.
It's cold, so the dog stays in its bed.
It's cold, so the dog stays in it's bed.
Its cold, so the dog stays in it's bed.
questions.explanation: It's is short for it is, which fits It's cold. Its with no apostrophe shows ownership, which fits its bed.

questions.stem: By noon, Lena had ___ across the whole lake. Which word or words best complete the sentence?
questions.explanation: After had, use the past participle swum. Swam is the simple past, used without a helping verb.

questions.stem: The game was paused during the storm. ___ the rain stopped, it started again. Which word or words best join the ideas?
questions.explanation: The game started again right after the rain stopped, so the words need to show time: as soon as. Even though would set up a contrast that is not there.

questions.stem: Which word means the same as **feeble**?
questions.explanation: Feeble means lacking strength, so it means weak. A feeble excuse is a weak one too.

questions.stem: **Praise** is the opposite of:
questions.explanation: To praise is to say good things about someone; to criticize is to point out faults. Celebrate and encourage are both close to praise.

questions.stem: **Tranquil** most nearly means:
questions.explanation: A tranquil lake has no waves or noise, so tranquil means calm and peaceful. A tranquil place is not necessarily cold or dull.

questions.stem: Which word means the opposite of **rigid**?
questions.explanation: Something rigid does not bend; something flexible bends easily. Unbending means the same as rigid.

questions.stem: **Sculptor** is to **clay** as **carpenter** is to:
questions.explanation: A sculptor shapes clay, and a carpenter shapes wood. A hammer and a saw are a carpenter's tools, not the material.

questions.stem: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: An eagle, a hawk and an owl are all birds. A bat flies too, but it is a mammal.

questions.stem: Ben is older than Cal but younger than Dee. Ed is older than Dee. Ben is younger than Ed. If the first two statements are true, the third statement is:
questions.explanation: From youngest to oldest the order is Cal, Ben, Dee, Ed. Ben is younger than Dee, and Dee is younger than Ed, so Ben is younger than Ed.

questions.stem: **Prudent** most nearly means:
questions.explanation: A prudent person thinks ahead and makes wise, sensible choices, such as saving money. Stubborn means unwilling to change one's mind.

questions.stem: **Hinder** is the opposite of:
questions.explanation: To hinder is to get in the way of something, so the opposite is to help. Delay and block are ways of hindering.

questions.stem: Which word means the same as **elated**?
questions.explanation: Elated means extremely happy, or overjoyed. Someone may be surprised and elated at once, but surprise is a different feeling.

questions.stem: Which word means the opposite of **opaque**?
questions.explanation: Light cannot pass through something opaque; it passes straight through something transparent, like clear glass. Dark-tinted glass is closer to opaque.

questions.stem: Compare (I) 1/3 of 27, (II) 1/2 of 16 and (III) 1/5 of 40. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 1/3 of 27 is 9, 1/2 of 16 is 8 and 1/5 of 40 is 8. So I is greatest and II equals III.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 100, 91, 82, 73, ...?
questions.explanation: Each number is 9 less than the one before it: 73 - 9 = 64.

questions.stem: In an isosceles triangle, the two equal angles are each 50°. Compare (I) the third angle, (II) one of the equal angles and (III) 90°. Which is true?
questions.explanation: The third angle is 180 - 50 - 50 = 80°. So III (90°) > I (80°) > II (50°).

questions.stem: What number is 6 more than the square of 5?
questions.explanation: The square of 5 is 5 × 5 = 25, and 25 + 6 = 31. Doubling 5 instead of squaring it gives 16.

questions.stem: Compare (I) 60% of 50, (II) 50% of 60 and (III) 25% of 100. Which is true?
questions.explanation: 60% of 50 and 50% of 60 are both 30, because 0.6 × 50 = 0.5 × 60. 25% of 100 is 25.

questions.stem: What number should come next in this series: 3, 5, 9, 15, 23, ...?
questions.explanation: The gaps are 2, 4, 6 and 8, growing by 2 each time. The next gap is 10, so 23 + 10 = 33.

questions.stem: Compare (I) the perimeter of a regular hexagon with 4 cm sides, (II) the perimeter of a square with 6 cm sides and (III) the perimeter of an equilateral triangle with 7 cm sides. Which is true?
questions.explanation: The hexagon is 6 × 4 = 24 cm, the square 4 × 6 = 24 cm and the triangle 3 × 7 = 21 cm. So I and II are equal and both greater than III.

questions.stem: Compare (I) the square root of 49, (II) 1 less than the square root of 64 and (III) 2 × 4. Which is true?
questions.explanation: The square root of 49 is 7, the square root of 64 is 8, so 1 less is 7, and 2 × 4 = 8. So III is greatest and I equals II.

questions.stem: What number is 4 less than 3/8 of 64?
What number should come next in this series: 1, 2, 6, 24, ...?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 2, then 3, then 4, then 5: 24 × 5 = 120. Doubling 24 to get 48 repeats only the first step.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12 units long. Compare (I) its hypotenuse, (II) the sum of its legs and (III) twice its shorter leg. Which is true?
questions.explanation: By the Pythagorean theorem the hypotenuse is 13 (25 + 144 = 169). The legs add to 17 and twice the shorter leg is 10. So 17 > 13 > 10.

questions.stem: Compare (I) (-2)², (II) -(2²) and (III) (-2) × (-2). Which is true?
questions.explanation: (-2)² = (-2) × (-2) = 4, so I and III are both 4. -(2²) is the negative of 4, which is -4.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __rapid__ river"?
questions.explanation: A rapid river moves quickly, so rapid means fast.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __repair__ the fence"?
questions.explanation: To repair something is to fix it. Building a fence would mean making a new one.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __humid__ afternoon"?
questions.explanation: Humid air holds a lot of moisture, which makes the day feel muggy. A humid day may be sunny, so it is not necessarily cloudy.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __consume__ the snack"?
questions.explanation: To consume food is to eat it.

questions.stem: How does Mateo feel about his new town during the first week?
questions.explanation: He spends the week glaring at the gray sky, and at the end the town finally feels less far from home. That shows he felt unhappy before.

questions.stem: The phrase "every fence post wore a tall white hat" is an example of:
questions.explanation: Fence posts cannot really wear hats; giving an object a human action is personification. The phrase describes the snow piled on top of each post.

questions.stem: What does the wave between Mateo and the girl most likely suggest?
options: He may make a friend there
He knew her from his old town
She wants him to go inside
She is asking for his help
questions.explanation: Right after the wave, the town starts to feel less far from home, which hints at a new friendship. Nothing suggests they had met before.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __hasty__ decision"?
questions.explanation: A hasty decision is made too quickly, so it is rushed. A hasty decision may not be wise.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __scrutinize__ the map"?
questions.explanation: To scrutinize something is to examine it very closely.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "a __docile__ pony"?
questions.explanation: A docile animal is calm and easy to handle, so docile means gentle. Wild is the opposite.

questions.stem: Which word means about the same as the underlined word in "to __concur__ with the coach"?
questions.explanation: To concur is to agree. Arguing with the coach would be the opposite.

questions.stem: What is 5/8 - 1/4?
questions.explanation: 1/4 = 2/8, so 5/8 - 2/8 = 3/8. Subtracting tops and bottoms to get 4/4 does not work.

questions.stem: What is 0.375 as a fraction in lowest terms?
questions.explanation: 0.375 = 375/1000, and dividing the top and bottom by 125 gives 3/8. 5/8 is 0.625.

questions.stem: How many positive factors does 18 have?
questions.explanation: The factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9 and 18, which is 6 in all. Forgetting 1 and 18 gives 4.

questions.stem: Two angles are supplementary. One measures 38°. What is the measure of the other?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add to 180°, so the other is 180 - 38 = 142°. 52° would make them complementary, adding to 90°.

questions.stem: If y/4 - 3 = 2, what is the value of y?
questions.explanation: Add 3 to both sides to get y/4 = 5, then multiply by 4: y = 20. Stopping at 5 forgets to multiply.

questions.stem: A spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability of landing on a number greater than 5?
questions.explanation: The numbers greater than 5 are 6, 7 and 8, so 3 of the 8 sections win: 3/8. 5/8 counts the numbers from 1 to 5 instead.

questions.stem: On a map, 1 inch stands for 20 miles. Two towns are 3.5 inches apart on the map. How far apart are they?
questions.explanation: Multiply: 3.5 × 20 = 70 miles. Adding 3.5 and 20 gives 23.5, which mixes up the operation.

questions.stem: Which shows 0.00052 in scientific notation?
questions.explanation: Move the decimal point four places to the right to get 5.2, so the power of ten is 10⁻⁴. A positive exponent would make a number larger than 1.

questions.stem: Which sentence uses capital letters correctly?
options: In the Fall, Ana will study Spanish.
In the fall, Ana will study spanish.
In the fall, Ana will study Spanish.
In the Fall, Ana will study spanish.
questions.explanation: Seasons are not capitalized, but the names of languages always are.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Library has an r after the b: li-brar-y.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.explanation: To show that one person owns something, add an apostrophe and s: Mia's. A question ends with a question mark.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: February has an r after the b and ends in -uary: Feb-ru-ar-y.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Here is the keys you lost.
Here are the keys you lost.
Here was the keys you lost.
questions.explanation: In a sentence that begins with here, the subject comes after the verb. Keys is plural, so the verb must be are.

questions.stem: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Our class likes hiking, swimming and to bike.
Our class likes to hike, swimming and biking.
Our class likes hiking, to swim and biking.
Our class likes hiking, swimming and biking.
questions.explanation: Items in a list should have the same form. Hiking, swimming and biking all end in -ing; mixing in to bike or to swim breaks the pattern.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: On May 4, 2026, the school held a fair.
On May 4 2026, the school held a fair.
On May, 4, 2026 the school held a fair.
On May 4, 2026 the school, held a fair.
questions.explanation: A full date in the middle of a sentence takes a comma after the day and after the year.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Definitely comes from finite, so it is spelled de-fin-ite-ly, with no a.

questions.stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: Mr. Patel our coach, gave a speech.
Mr. Patel, our coach gave a speech.
Mr. Patel our coach gave, a speech.
Mr. Patel, our coach, gave a speech.
questions.explanation: Our coach renames Mr. Patel, so it needs a comma on both sides. Leaving out either comma breaks the pair.

questions.stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Occurred has a double c and a double r. The r doubles because occur is stressed on its last syllable.
